source_text:
3.34 Ἀφρικανοῦ· εἰς τὸ πραῦναι <φλεγμονὰς ποδῶν> καὶ
ἄλλων μερῶν Φοίνικας ζʹ προβρέξας ἐν οἴνῳ γλυκεῖ ἕως ἁπαλοὶ γένωνται τρῖβε σὺν
ἀρκοῦντι ῥοδίνῳ ὡς λειότατα. Εἶτα κηροῦ καὶ στέατος χοιρείου προσφάτου καὶ
ψιχῶν ἄρτου ἴσα σὺν ῥοδίνῳ ἑψήσας μικρὸν κατὰ τῶν λελειωμένων φοινίκων
ἐπίχει καὶ ἑνώσας ἐν θυίᾳ ποίει ὑγρὸν ὡς ἐμπλαστρῶδες καὶ ἐπιθεὶς τὴν φλεγμονὴν
εὐθὺς ἀρεῖς.
pass_a_gloss: 3.34 Of-Africanus: into the to-soothe <inflammations of-feet> and of-other parts. Dates 7 having-soaked-first in wine sweet until soft they-become rub with sufficient rose-oil as most-smooth. Then of-wax and of-fat of-hog fresh and of-crumbs of-bread equals with rose-oil having-boiled a-little upon the having-been-smoothed dates pour and having-united in a-mortar make wet as plaster-like and having-applied the inflammation at-once you-will-take-away.
pass_b_english: Of Africanus: to soothe inflammations of the feet and of other parts. Having first soaked seven dates in sweet wine until they become soft, rub them with sufficient rose-oil as smoothly as possible. Then, having boiled a little equal parts of wax, fresh hog's fat, and bread-crumbs with rose-oil, pour them over the smoothed dates; having united them in a mortar, make the mixture wet as a plaster, and having applied it you will take the inflammation away at once.

choices.why: ζʹ is 7. Stigma/digamma is 6. Not six dates.
θύεια is a mortar. Not incense (θυμίαμα).
προβρέχω is soak beforehand, then τρῖβε rub. Not 'having rubbed' twice.
rejected: having boiled the dates in wine

anf_compare.notes: No PD English of the Cesti body; ANF has the letters only.
